Evaluation details

Metric. Recall@k measures gold-paper coverage among the first k results; Recall@All uses the full ranking at termination. Scores are query-level macro means. arXiv versions are merged and duplicate papers retain their earliest rank.

Systems. All 1,111 queries: Method (302), Setting (322), Scope (317), and Comparison (170). Agent results are means over three runs. Retrieval and agentic systems use ScholarBase; external services use their own indexes and return at most 300 papers. Original system budgets and stopping rules are retained; this is not a matched-budget comparison. Other systems' repeat counts are not specified in the manuscript.

Model configurations. ScholarQuest-100 contains 25 queries per intent. All configurations share the search harness, with up to 15 rounds and 5 parallel tool calls per round. Failed or incomplete queries and invalid token records are excluded. Valid query sets differ; overall scores are means over each configuration's valid queries. Prompts and inference settings vary, including a dedicated GPT-5.6-Sol keyword-search prompt.

Planner tokens. Configuration details report mean input + output tokens from the final successful Planner attempt. Selector usage, failed attempts and preflight requests are excluded. Reasoning is counted once within completion tokens. Tokenizers differ; these figures do not measure billing cost.

About

ScholarQuest evaluates whether paper-search systems can satisfy explicit research constraints, beyond matching a topic. Queries cover four intents: a required method, a research setting, an inclusion or exclusion scope, and a comparative finding.

The benchmark spans 355 topic labels and 36 arXiv computer-science categories. Gold relevance is grounded in titles, abstracts and metadata; coverage is not guaranteed to be exhaustive. A missing gold match does not by itself establish irrelevance.
